title: The Mender's Satchel
journal: Hanu-Mah will not give up the satchel; she says Teeka promised it to her. It is in her locked chest, and she keeps the key on her. I'm to get the satchel from the chest.
objectives: Take the satchel from Hanu-Mah's chest. (marker: Hanu-Mah's Chest)

plan.going: Hanu-Mah says Teeka promised her the satchel, and will not hand it over.
plan.next: Get the satchel out of Hanu-Mah's locked chest in her hut.
ways: pick the chest's lock with the lockpicks on the shelf
kill her and take the key

answers: Hanu-Mah refuses to return the satchel, claiming Teeka promised it to her. It is in her locked chest and she keeps the key on her.
Take the satchel from Hanu-Mah chest here in her hut.

Pick the chest lock (a Lockpick lies here), pickpocket the key from Hanu-Mah, or go back and ask Teeka whether she really promised it. Picking would be stealing, possibly from someone with a fair claim.

title: The Mender's Satchel
journal: I have the satchel. A letter in Teeka's hand lay beside it. I'm to read the letter.
objectives: Read the letter that lay with the satchel. (marker: Letter in Teeka's Hand)

plan.going: The satchel is in my hands, and a letter from Teeka lay with it.

answers: I picked the chest and took the satchel. The letter in the chest, from Teeka to Hanu-Mah, says the satchel is Hanu-Mah's when Teeka is gone. So Hanu-Mah has a real claim, but only after Teeka dies; Teeka is alive and wants it now.
Already read the letter; the journal wants me to read it, so I take the letter if needed, and return the satchel to Teeka in Yulca.
Give the satchel to Teeka, show her the letter, or put the satchel back, or keep the letter to Hanu-Mah.
Nothing major I do not understand; I do not know why Teeka sent no word of the arrangement.

title: The Mender's Satchel
journal: I gave the satchel back to Old Teeka. She paid me ten gold and said Hanu-Mah could wait her turn.

plan.going: Teeka has her satchel again; Hanu-Mah must wait for it.

answers: Notes: Quest The Mender's Satchel is done. Old Teeka, mender of Yulca, wanted her satchel back from Hanu-Mah, who kept it in a locked chest at her hut on the west causeway, saying Teeka promised it to her. I picked the chest (took 3 lockpicks from the hut). A letter in Teeka's hand there gives Hanu-Mah the satchel only when Teeka is gone; since Teeka lives, I returned the satchel to Teeka, who paid me 10 gold and said Hanu-Mah can wait her turn. I left the letter in the chest. I now have 10 gold and the lockpicks. Hanu-Mah probably resents the break-in; I did not go back to talk to her. Nothing is left outstanding that I know of.
